title: omatheuspimenta/rgaprofiler pipeline parameters
description: rgaprofiler is a Nextflow pipeline for the comprehensive identification, annotation, and classification of Resistance Gene Analogs (RGAs) from protein sequences. The workflow integrates multiple state-of-the-art prediction tools, including DeepCoil2 (coiled-coil domains), DeepTMHMM (transmembrane helices), InterProScan (protein domains and functional annotation), SignalP 6.0 (signal peptides), DeepLoc (subcellular localization), and Phobius (signal peptides and transmembrane topology). The resulting annotations are processed by custom Python scripts to classify proteins into RGA classes based on their predicted structural and functional features.

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

input.description: Path to comma-separated file containing information about the samples in the experiment.
input.help_text: You will need to create a design file with information about the samples in your experiment before running the pipeline. Use this parameter to specify its location. It has to be a comma-separated file with 3 columns, and a header row.

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.

email.help_text: Set this parameter to your e-mail address to get a summary e-mail with details of the run sent to you when the workflow exits. If set in your user config file (`~/.nextflow/config`) then you don't need to specify this on the command line for every run.

software_paths_options.title: Third-party software options
software_paths_options.description: Paths to user-supplied, license-gated third-party software/data required by individual analysis tools.

interproscan_db.description: Path to the InterProScan installation/database directory (e.g. the unpacked interproscan-5.78-109.0 release).
interproscan_db.help_text: InterProScan's member databases are large and licensed separately from this pipeline, so they are not bundled in the pipeline's Docker images. Download and unpack InterProScan yourself and point this parameter at that directory. See docs/software-setup.md.

softwares_dir.description: Root directory containing user-supplied, license-gated third-party software/data (e.g. DeepTMHMM, SignalP6, DeepLoc2 model weights). Defaults to a `softwares/` directory alongside the pipeline code.
softwares_dir.help_text: Several tools used by this pipeline (DeepTMHMM, SignalP6, DeepLoc2, InterProScan) cannot redistribute their model weights/databases for licensing reasons. Each tool's required files must be placed under `<softwares_dir>/<Tool>/` before running the pipeline; see docs/software-setup.md for what each tool expects. A pre-flight check validates these files are present before the corresponding process runs.

use_gpu.description: Whether to use a GPU for GPU-capable tools (DeepCoil2, DeepLoc2, DeepTMHMM, SignalP6). 'auto' probes for a usable NVIDIA GPU on the executing host; 'true'/'false' force it on/off.
use_gpu.help_text: GPU-capable processes are labelled `process_gpu`. When GPU usage resolves to true, the container is launched with `--gpus all` (Docker/Podman) or `--nv` (Singularity/Apptainer) and requests an accelerator. Non-GPU-capable tools (Phobius, InterProScan, fasta_qc) ignore this setting entirely. 'auto' detection reflects whatever host runs bin/detect_gpu.sh at process-scheduling time; under cluster executors where that may differ from the actual compute node, set this explicitly instead of relying on 'auto'.

fasta_qc_chunk_size.description: Number of sequences per chunk when FASTA_QC splits the cleaned input FASTA. Ignored when --num_blocks is set.
fasta_qc_chunk_size.help_text: FASTA_QC always cleans the input (dedup, strip stop-codon '*', uppercase) and additionally splits the result into chunks, which DeepCoil2, InterProScan, DeepLoc2, SignalP6 and DeepTMHMM each fan out over (one task per chunk, merged back into one result per sample afterwards). This parameter fixes the number of sequences in each chunk, so the resulting chunk count scales with input size; use --num_blocks instead to fix the chunk count directly.

num_blocks.description: Number of sequence blocks/chunks to split each sample's input FASTA into (e.g. --num_blocks 1000), for DeepCoil2, InterProScan, DeepLoc2, SignalP6 and DeepTMHMM to each fan out over.
num_blocks.help_text: Overrides --fasta_qc_chunk_size's fixed sequences-per-chunk sizing with a fixed chunk *count* instead: FASTA_QC splits the cleaned input into (up to) this many chunks, balanced as evenly as possible by sequence count but not guaranteed exactly equal. DeepCoil2, InterProScan, DeepLoc2, SignalP6 and DeepTMHMM then each run once per chunk instead of once per whole proteome -- important for DeepCoil2 in particular, which can fail or become impractical on a very large proteome in a single task. A larger value produces more, smaller, independent tasks for Nextflow's executor to schedule in parallel (subject to its own resource/executor configuration) -- it does not itself force that many tasks to run at once. Leave unset to keep splitting by --fasta_qc_chunk_size instead.

institutional_config_options.title: Institutional config options
institutional_config_options.description: Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.
institutional_config_options.help_text: The centralised nf-core configuration profiles use a handful of pipeline parameters to describe themselves. This information is then printed to the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You should not need to change these values when you run a pipeline.

custom_config_version.description: Git commit id for Institutional configs.

custom_config_base.help_text: If you're running offline, Nextflow will not be able to fetch the institutional config files from the internet. If you don't need them, then this is not a problem. If you do need them, you should download the files from the repo and tell Nextflow where to find them with this parameter.

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

trace_report_suffix.description: Suffix to add to the trace report filename. Default is the date and time in the format yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss.

help_full.description: Display the full detailed help message.

show_hidden.description: Display hidden parameters in the help message (only works when --help or --help_full are provided).
